description:
fz-qe0 (recursive-group walk no longer steps into settled products) sped every Enum-heavy fixture up. Several timeout overrides that existed to accommodate the old cost are now dead weight -- an override far above the real cost is a disabled detector.

MEASURED at fz-qe0 HEAD, debug build, unloaded machine (interp / run / build):
  enum_tier0                  0.7 / 0.9 / 0.9 s   -- override: interp 15s   => REMOVE, default 3s covers it
  fz_f98_range_map_converges  0.8 / 1.0 / 1.0 s   -- override: interp 15s   => REMOVE, default 3s covers it
  enum_map_family             2.1 / 2.8 / 2.9 s   -- override: 15/15/15     => LOWER (near the 3s default; keep headroom)
  enum_take_drop_split        4.4 / 5.3 / 5.4 s   -- override: 15/15/15     => LOWER to ~8s
  enum_predicate_search       2.6 / 3.1 / 3.1 s   -- already lowered to 6/6 by fz-qe0

Lowering a budget is safe by construction (a stricter guard), so this needs no masked-regression scrutiny -- only a check that output stays correct. Re-measure before choosing numbers: these were taken on one unloaded machine and CI may be slower, so leave real headroom rather than trimming to the measurement.

SEPARATE FINDING, fix it here: fixtures2/behavior/enum_tier0.fz says 'The interp timeout override is temporary; fz-g58.52 owns restoring the default'. There is no fz-g58.52 -- 'bw show fz-g58.52' reports no such issue. The pointer is dangling, so the override had no live owner. Point the fixture at this ticket or drop the sentence with the override.

comments.text:
OBSOLETE at main 417c5b0b5 -- this ticket's prescription is now actively wrong, and its one live remnant is fixed.

## The prescription no longer holds

This says 'an override far above the real cost is a disabled detector' and asks
to REMOVE enum_tier0's and fz_f98_range_map_converges's overrides (dropping them
to the 3s default) and LOWER the others.

Doing that would recreate the defect fz-f98.23 was filed to fix. A wall-clock
budget calibrated on dev hardware cannot gate CI: the runners are much slower and
run under llvm-cov instrumentation. enum_predicate_search's 6s cap -- which this
ticket cites approvingly as 'already lowered by fz-qe0' -- exceeded on EVERY CI
run of the fz-go4.1..fz-f98.24 stack and went unnoticed for eleven PRs. It is now
20s and documented as a hang backstop that is deliberately too loose to notice a
regression.

So tightening these overrides is the opposite of what the evidence supports. The
detector moves to a machine-independent work-count ceiling: fz-f98.23.

## The measurements are also stale

They were taken at fz-qe0 HEAD, before fz-6gb cut executable fanout ~5x on
lambda-heavy programs. Any re-derivation has to start from fresh numbers.

## The one live remnant is fixed

'enum_tier0 cites a ticket that no longer exists' was true and is now handled:
PR #104 repoints the deferral references in enum_tier0, fz_f98_map_reduce and
enum_predicate_search at the live fz-kdt tickets. That survey also found 57
ticket references across the fixture corpus naming tickets that no longer exist,
but those are provenance ('exercises the fz-g58.26 layer'), not actionable
pointers, and are deliberately left alone.

Closing. No successor: there is nothing left to do that fz-f98.23 does not
already own.

title: Retire the now-unneeded fixture timeout overrides (enum_tier0, fz_f98_range_map_converges); enum_tier0 cites a ticket that no longer exists
